title: dsh starts again after it died holding a writer lock: a lock its own PID left before this process started (a restarted container's PID 1) is taken over instead of failing startup
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node tests/regression/scripts/REG-PR-1100-p8-dsh-stale-own-pid-lock.mjs — it runs the fork's vitest over packages/util/atomic-write/tests/atomic-write.spec.ts in vendor/tracy/deepseek-harness (node_modules/.bin/vitest run … with a JSON report) and checks every test named below.
expect: S1: the spec exits 0 with no failed and no skipped test.

E2: 'takes over a lock its own PID left before this process started' and 'admits one contender at a time when several take over a lock its own PID left earlier' pass — a lock file recording this process's PID and last written before it started (what a container's PID 1 that ended mid-write leaves for its next run) is taken over at once (waitMs 0), the operation runs under a fresh lock, eight contenders never overlap, and no lock or claim file is left.

E3: 'keeps a lock this process holds even when its file looks older than the process', 'keeps a lock this process holds under another spelling of its path', 'keeps a lock another call of this process is still creating' and 'still times out a nested acquisition of the lock its caller holds' pass — a lock this module instance is creating or holds is waited for even when its file is made to look older than the process.

E4: 'waits for a lock another copy of this package took since this process started', 'waits for the lock of this process', 'keeps a lock rewritten under its own PID while this contender claimed the earlier one' and "waits for its own PID's earlier lock when the runtime cannot tell when it started" pass — an own-PID lock written since this process started is waited for.

E5: 'takes over a lock whose holder exited', 'takes over the lock of a process that really exited', 'waits for the lock of a live holder', 'waits for a holder whose process exists under another user' and 'keeps its own lock when the runtime cannot probe itself' pass — locks of other PIDs are judged as before.

selectors.acquisition: vendor/tracy/deepseek-harness/packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts withFileLock (enterLocal before the wx create, leaveLocal after the lock is removed)

evidence: Local stand 10/10/2026: after the Docker disk filled, tracy-dsh (node as PID 1, dsh 0.2.0-rc.2-tracy.37) failed startup on every restart with 'StartupError: dsh: startup failed: 1 required plugin did not activate … connection (required) … atomic-write: timed out waiting for the writer lock at /desk-home/.credentials.yaml.lock'; the lock held '1\n' (12 startup logs 07:39-07:45 UTC). Reproduced with real PID reuse in tasks/evidence/followups-2026-10-10/p8-dshlock/linux-pid1-restart.txt.
fence: Own-PID takeover needs both: no acquisition of this module instance is creating or holding the lock, and the lock file's mtime is before this process's start (Date.now() - process.uptime()). Not covered: a dead holder whose PID another live process reused (still waits, as before); a clock stepped back past the lock's write delays the takeover.
